question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[1,2]\times [1,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}y+x-3 \\ x{y}^{2}-y-1\end{aligned}]. $$ Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts at ${x}_{0}=[1,\,1]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[1,\,2]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).
${x}_{2}\,≈[$ $1.091$ $]$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y+x-3) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y+x-3) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}(x{y}^{2}-y-1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(x{y}^{2}-y-1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2xy+1 & {x}^{2} \\ {y}^{2} & 2xy-1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}2xy+1 & {x}^{2} \\ {y}^{2} & 2xy-1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}y+x-3 \\ x{y}^{2}-y-1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}2xy+1 & {x}^{2} \\ {y}^{2} & 2xy-1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}y+x-3 \\ x{y}^{2}-y-1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}2(1)(2)+1 & (1)^{2} \\ (2)^{2} & 2(1)(2)-1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}(1)^{2}(2)+(1)-3 \\ (1)(2)^{2}-(2)-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{5\cdot 3-1\cdot 4}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -4 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{11}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{12}{11} \\ \frac{17}{11}\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}1.091 \\ 1.545\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
